The DAFS Teaching App is a small program that runs on your own laptop and opens
in your web browser. It walks you through the course's R lessons: you read a
short explanation, write code in an editor, press **Run**, and get feedback
straight away.

You install and start the app from R itself, so everything happens in R and
RStudio, the same tools you use in the rest of the course.

This guide shows you how to install it, start it, and keep it up to date.

# What you need

- **R 4.1 or newer.** Open RStudio and look at the first line of the
  **Console** (the panel where R prints its output). It says something like
  `R version 4.4.1`. You can also type this in the Console and press Enter:

  ```r
  R.version.string
  ```

  If the version is 4.1 or higher, you're fine. If it's older, or you don't
  have R yet, install the latest version from
  [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org/).

- **RStudio.** Not strictly required, but strongly recommended: it's what we
  use in class. Download it for free from
  [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

- **An internet connection** for the installation. After that, the app works
  offline.

::: {.callout-note}
## Where do I type the commands?
All commands in this guide go in the RStudio **Console**: click in it, paste
the command, and press Enter. Don't put them in a script.
:::

# Installing the app

The app is not on CRAN (R's official package store), but on GitHub. To
install packages from GitHub, you first need a small helper package called
**remotes**. Run these two lines in the Console, one after the other:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("JPvdP/dafs-teach-r", dependencies = TRUE)
```

This downloads the app together with everything it needs, including the
**tidyverse** that the lessons use. If you don't have the tidyverse yet, this
can take several minutes the first time. You'll see a lot of text scrolling by:
that's normal.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Questions R may ask you during the installation
- **"These packages have more recent versions available. Which would you
  like to update?"** Type `3` (*None*) and press Enter. Updating everything
  takes a long time, and isn't needed for the app.
- **"Do you want to install from sources the packages which need
  compilation?"** Type `No` and press Enter.
:::

When the installation is finished, the Console shows the `>` prompt again,
and you can type a new command.

# Starting the app

In the Console, type:

```r
dafsteach::run_app()
```

After a few seconds the app opens, either in your web browser or in a window
from RStudio, depending on your RStudio settings. If it opens in a small panel
in RStudio, you can click **Show in new window** at the top of that panel, or
start the app like this to always open it in your browser:

```r
dafsteach::run_app(launch.browser = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The Console is busy while the app runs
While the app is running, R is busy: you'll see a red **Stop** sign at the top
of the Console, and you can't run other code there. When you're done, click
that red **Stop** sign, or click in the Console and press **Esc**. Closing
the browser tab does not stop the app.
:::

# Using the app

## The first time: enter your name

When you open the app for the first time it asks for your name.

::: {.callout-warning}
Use your **full name exactly as it appears on Brightspace**, and always use
the same spelling. Your completion codes (see below) are linked to this name,
so a typo or a nickname means your codes won't match.
:::

## Working through a lesson

1. On the home page, pick a lesson and click **Open**. Lessons are numbered in
   the order we cover them in class.
2. Read the instructions, then write your code in the editor.
3. Click **▶ Run** to run your code. You see what your code printed under
   **Output**, and whether your answer passes the checks under **Feedback**.
4. Stuck? Click **💡 Show hint** to reveal hints one at a time. Use
   **👁 Solution** only as a last resort — you learn far more by trying first.
5. Once an exercise passes, click **Next →** to go to the next one. Use the
   list of exercises on the left to jump between exercises, or **← Home** to go
   back to the list of lessons.

Your progress is saved automatically on your own computer, so you can stop
the app and carry on later where you left off.

::: {.callout-note}
## Messages and warnings are not errors
Some code prints extra information, for example the list of packages when you
load the tidyverse, or the column types after reading a file. The app shows
this in grey under **Messages and warnings**. Only a real **error** (shown in
red) means your code stopped.
:::

## "Explain this script" exercises

In some lessons you don't write code: you read a script and explain in your own
words what it does, just like on the exam. Write your explanation in the
editor, and click **📝 Submit explanation**. The app checks that your
explanation is long enough, and then shows a **model answer** to compare yours
with. Be honest with yourself: did you spot everything the model answer
mentions?

## Getting your completion code

When you've finished **every** exercise in a lesson, open the home page and
click **🎓 Get completion code** on that lesson's card. Upload this code to
Brightspace as proof you completed the module.

# Updating the app

New lessons and fixes are added during the course. When we announce an update,
stop the app (red **Stop** sign) and run the installation command again:

```r
remotes::install_github("JPvdP/dafs-teach-r", dependencies = TRUE)
```

Then start the app again with `dafsteach::run_app()`. Your progress is kept.

::: {.callout-tip}
If R says that **dafsteach** is in use and asks you to restart R, click
**Yes**. You can also restart R yourself first, via *Session → Restart R* in
RStudio.
:::

# Good to know

- **Your code runs separately.** The app runs your code in a separate R
  session, so variables you create in the app don't appear in RStudio's
  **Environment** panel, and code in the app can't break your own work. If
  your code runs for more than 10 seconds (for example an endless loop), the
  app stops it.
- **Where is my progress stored?** In a folder on your own computer. You can
  see exactly where by running `tools::R_user_dir("dafsteach", "data")`.
  Nothing about you is uploaded anywhere.
- **Anonymous progress reports.** After a weekly deadline has passed, the app
  may send your instructor an *anonymous* summary of how the class did on that
  week's exercises (for example, how many attempts an exercise took). Your name
  is never included. You'll see a small notice when this happens.
- **Settings from your instructor.** If your instructor asks you to set a
  variable such as `DAFS_TEACH_SECRET` before starting the app, follow their
  instructions exactly. If you haven't been told to, you don't need to do
  anything.

# Troubleshooting

**`there is no package called 'remotes'`**
: You skipped the first installation line. Run
  `install.packages("remotes")` first, then the `install_github()` line again.

**`there is no package called 'dafsteach'`**
: The installation didn't finish. Scroll up in the Console to find the first
  line that starts with `Error`, and run the installation command again. If it
  fails a second time, bring that error message to the lab session.

**An error mentioning `API rate limit exceeded` or `HTTP error 403`**
: GitHub limits how often one network can download from it. This happens when
  many students install at the same time on the same Wi-Fi. Wait a few
  minutes, or try again from home.

**An error saying a package requires a newer version of R**
: Your R is too old. Install the latest version from
  [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org/), restart RStudio, and
  install the app again.

**The app doesn't open, or the page stops responding**
: Check the Console in RStudio. If there's no red **Stop** sign, the app isn't
  running any more: start it again with `dafsteach::run_app()`.

**An exercise says `there is no package called 'tidyverse'`**
: The tidyverse didn't get installed along with the app. Stop the app, run
  `install.packages("tidyverse")`, and start the app again.

**Something else?**
: Copy the full error message from the Console and bring it to the lab
  session, or post it on the course forum on Brightspace.
